transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably just a quirk, really. But... well, I've been having a little trouble just staying in my chair lately. 

I keep getting up when I'm really supposed to just stay put. Like, I'll be right in the middle of a client interview—I'm a private investigator, so listening is important—or doing a tutoring session, or even just sitting with friends at my book club, and I just sort of... pop up. I try to play it off like I just needed to stretch, but people are definitely starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, that I can't just be polite and stay seated. 

Does that... does that make sense as a reason to come in? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you feel a constant restlessness or urge to move even when you're not physically uncomfortable or trying to be polite?

Oh... um, well, I guess you could call it that? I always just try to look at it as being highly motivated, if that makes sense. I hope that doesn't sound defensive! But... yes, I suppose even when I'm perfectly comfortable, I just can't seem to stop going. 

Like, on days when I don't have any actual field work and I'm supposed to be relaxing, I still end up bouncing around. I'll start unpacking boxes, and then I'll move right into reorganizing my old case files, and before I know it I'm out the door running errands like I'm actively chasing a lead or something. I just... I have a really hard time just being off duty. I always feel like I need to be doing *something*. 

I hope it's okay that I'm like that—I know it's good to be productive, but I guess it is a little exhausting sometimes. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant?
Do you ever find it hard to focus or stay attentive, even when you're trying your best to concentrate on something important?

Um... actually, no, I don't think I really struggle with that part. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging or anything! But, well, with my line of work, I really have to stay sharp and catch the little details. I feel like I'm actually pretty good at locking in when something is important. 

My body might want to be moving, but my mind is usually right there, focused on the case or the person in front of me. So... no, I haven't really noticed any trouble paying attention. 

Is it okay that I don't have that issue? I know you're asking for a reason, and I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information to help you figure this out.
Have you ever found yourself acting on impulse, like making sudden decisions or interrupting others, without really thinking about it first?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I hope that doesn't make me sound rude or anything, because I really do try to be considerate of others. But, um, sometimes... I just get so enthusiastic about helping, you know? 

Like, if I'm at the precinct and I overhear some of the junior detectives trying to work out a lead, or even if it's just my neighbor out in the hallway talking about something... I kind of just jump right in. I'll start asking questions or offering advice before they've even invited me into the conversation. It's just because I really want to be helpful and share what I know! But then, a few minutes later, I'll realize I completely barged in where I wasn't asked. 

I always feel awful about it afterward, and I hope people know my heart is in the right place. Does that... does that sound like what you're asking about? I really hope I'm not coming across as too overbearing.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about things, even when there isn't an immediate reason to be concerned?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I hope that's an okay answer! But I don't really consider myself an anxious person. 

I guess sometimes I get a little... keyed up, maybe? But it's usually just because I'm eager to get things done or follow up on something for a client. It's more of an energetic feeling than a worried one, if that makes sense. I really try to stay positive and focus on solving the problem in front of me rather than sitting around fretting about things. 

I know some people worry a lot, and I totally understand why they do, but I just... I don't really have that issue. Is it helpful that I don't? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Um... no, I wouldn't say I've ever felt like that. I hope that's the right kind of answer! But, well... I've always been an energetic person, you know? It's just my baseline. I don't really have these... unusual spikes where I suddenly don't need sleep or my thoughts are going a million miles an hour. 

I mean, if I'm working a big case, I might stay up late because I'm just so invested in finding the answer, but I still *want* to sleep. And I definitely need it! I'm not superhuman or anything. 

So... no, I haven't really experienced those kinds of periods. I just have my regular, everyday high energy. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not throwing off your evaluation by not having these things you're asking about.
Have you ever felt unusually tired or slowed down, either in your body or your thoughts, especially when you’re not actively working on something?

Oh, um... no. Not really. I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to these things! I promise I'm really trying to give you the best answers, I just want to make sure I'm being accurate. 

Even when I don't have an active investigation going on, I don't really feel... sluggish or weighed down. I mean, I might have a quiet afternoon where I'm not running around, but my mind is usually still going. I'll be thinking about old cases, or organizing my files, or just figuring out what I need to do around the house. 

I get normal tired at the end of a long day, of course, just like anybody else. But I don't ever get that heavy, slowed-down feeling in my body or my thoughts. I really prefer to keep moving and stay productive, you know? 

I hope that's a helpful answer... am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your evaluation.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat when you're expected to sit still for a period of time?

Um... well, I guess I do move around a little bit? I mean, I hope that's not a bad thing! I try really hard to stay focused. 

But, you know, when I'm stuck at the computer for hours, just combing through endless public records or financial statements... it gets a little tedious. So, yeah, sometimes my foot will be bouncing under the desk, or I might be clicking a pen. I don't mean to be disruptive or anything! It's just a way to keep my energy up while I work. 

Sometimes I'll shift around in my chair a bit, and... well, occasionally I might shift so much that I lose my place in what I'm reading. But I always find it again! I'm still getting the work done. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm not taking my job seriously. It's just a little bit of restless energy. Is it normal to do that when you're sitting for a long time? I just want to make sure I'm answering this right for you.
Have these behaviors ever caused you any real problems at work, in your relationships, or in other important parts of your life?

Oh, um... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a bad investigator, because I do love my job and I try so hard to be good at it. But... I guess maybe it has caused a few little hiccups? 

I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but... sometimes, because I'm moving so fast or trying to get through things quickly, I might have missed a detail here or there in an investigation. Nothing completely catastrophic, I promise! Just... things I should have caught the first time around. 

And, um... well, I guess I can get a little overenthusiastic when I'm talking to clients or colleagues. I just have so many thoughts I want to share! But I think I might have irritated a few clients by jumping in too much. And... the junior detectives... well, they've been a little less willing to debrief with me lately. I think they feel a bit steamrolled when I get going. I feel just terrible about it, I really don't mean to talk over them! 

So, I suppose it is starting to cost me a little bit professionally. I hope you don't think poorly of me for that! I really am trying to work on it. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
